solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Prisoner's place of internment

definitions.meaning: read cryptically as '...', a lag being British slang for a convict
a German camp for captured officers in wartime

explanation.walkthrough: 'Prisoner's' is split as 'of' plus LAG, British slang for a convict, so the possessive spells the camp's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word was the German name for a prisoner-of-war camp holding captured officers.

clue.text: One Pole is so ecstatic?

definitions.meaning: the North Pole sits at the very top of the globe

explanation.walkthrough: 'One Pole' looks like a Polish person; it is the North Pole, literally sitting at the summit of the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone feeling elated, as if perched at the peak of everything.

clue.text: Some cruel, ungentlemanly attack

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A description of a brutish, unsporting assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden forward thrust, as in fencing, is a kind of attack.

clue.text: Awarded sum of money, teachers' leaders accepted

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a grand is a thousand pounds
the leading letters, the first two, of the word teachers

explanation.surface: A cash award is announced, with the heads of the teaching staff going along with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' here takes the first two letters, not just one. 'Accepted' looks like a second definition but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something granted has been bestowed or conferred, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Pregnant partner no longer has therapy wearing short trousers

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the therapy goes inside the clothing
short means cut, so the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: pants is an informal word for trousers
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.surface: A mother-to-be's former partner is in therapy dressed in shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the trousers by one letter, giving PANT, and 'wearing' puts the therapy inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An expectant mother is one awaiting a baby, a common euphemism.

clue.text: No introduction for brief broadcast

indicators.note: no introduction means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a remit is a brief, a set of instructions

explanation.surface: A short programme goes out without any opening announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No introduction for' removes the R from REMIT. 'Brief' looks like an adjective meaning short, but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or transmit, as a signal is sent out.

clue.text: Ambassador having only women admitted into China? That's incredible

indicators.note: admitted into means placed inside, so these go within the friend

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal
HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title
only women means no men

explanation.surface: An envoy lets only women into China, an astonishing policy.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate. HE stands for His Excellency.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomenal means extraordinary, beyond belief, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Nick minor works penned by hack

definitions.note: British slang for a police station

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the works go inside

parts.note: to hack is to chop
ops, opuses, are works; small ones in this sense

explanation.surface: A small-time thief steals minor items and a journalist writes it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a verb meaning steal; in British slang it is a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: The nick is British slang for a police station, also called a cop shop.

clue.text: Dispute stated intention of Petruchio?

indicators.note: stated means spoken, so we want what the words sound like

parts.note: in The Taming of the Shrew, Petruchio aims to change Kate, to alter Kate

explanation.surface: An argument about what Shakespeare's Petruchio meant to do.
explanation.walkthrough: Petruchio sets out to tame the shrewish Kate in The Taming of the Shrew: 'alter Kate', which said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To altercate is to argue heatedly, to quarrel.

clue.text: What could make you fitter? Extremely delicious beans on toast

indicators.note: the answer's letters could be made, rearranged, from these pieces
extremely means taking the outermost letters of the word

explanation.surface: A query about getting fit, then a breakfast of tasty beans on toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toast' looks like the bread under the beans; it is a raised-glass salute. The anagram is of FITTER, DS (the ends of 'delicious'), BEANS and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional salute raised in memory of companions who cannot be present.

clue.text: Provisional accommodation this setter's found after a time

indicators.note: found after says the setter's piece follows the a-and-time piece

parts.note: a tent is camping accommodation
the setter speaking in the first person: I have, shortened

explanation.surface: The setter has found some temporary lodging after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This setter's' stands for I'VE, the compiler saying 'I have'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tentative means provisional, not yet final, a synonym.

clue.text: Odd sections of 11 road in old city

indicators.note: odd sections are the first, third and fifth letters

parts.note: the answer to 11 across, meaning quite

explanation.surface: Strange stretches of a road in an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' points to the answer to 11 across; take its odd letters, then those of 'road'.
explanation.definitionFit: Petra is the ancient rock-cut city in Jordan.

clue.text: Quite dry inside quarry

indicators.note: inside means placed within the hunted animal

parts.note: quarry is the hunted animal, the prey
TT means teetotal, not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A quarry that is fairly dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarry' looks like a stone pit; it is hunted prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty can mean fairly or rather, as in pretty good.

clue.text: Divers fish in schools

indicators.note: in puts the fish inside the schools

parts.note: pods are schools of whales or dolphins
char is a fish of the trout family

explanation.surface: Swimmers hunting fish among schools of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' looks like people; they are diving ducks.
explanation.definitionFit: The pochard is a diving duck, so pochards are examples of divers.

clue.text: Mike accompanies one foreign gent around a group of islands

parts.note: mike and mic are both short for microphone

indicators.note: around means the one-and-gent pair is turned back to front

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
senor is Spanish for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A man named Mike travels with a foreign gentleman around an archipelago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mike' looks like the NATO letter M; it is a microphone. 'around' turns one + gent into RONESI.
explanation.definitionFit: Micronesia is a Pacific region made up of thousands of small islands.

clue.text: Maybe Nietzsche ultimately rejected English food

indicators.note: the last letter is thrown out

parts.note: Nietzsche's first name was Friedrich, so he is one example of it

explanation.surface: The philosopher Nietzsche turned down English cooking in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately rejected' drops the final H of FRIEDRICH.
explanation.definitionFit: Fried rice is a dish, a familiar example of food.

clue.text: Doctor in Lima is a member of religious sect

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician in Peru's capital belongs to a religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a physician; it is a verb, to tamper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ismailis are a branch of Shia Islam; an Ismailian is a follower.

clue.text: The reverse of mountain home here?

definitions.text: The reverse of mountain home here?

indicators.note: the reverse of means the mountain word is read backwards

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
in means at home

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where to live: the opposite of a mountain home.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, a flat expanse is the opposite of a mountain, and somewhere people make a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain is flat land, the opposite of a mountain.

clue.text: Honour received by female poet

indicators.note: received by means taken inside the female word

parts.note: her refers to a female
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A woman writer accepts an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer is the ancient Greek epic writer of the Iliad and Odyssey.

clue.text: Admonish salesman about promoting first of remnants

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: promoting means moving up, so a letter is shifted forward

parts.note: over can mean about, as in a row over money

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of remnants

explanation.surface: A boss tells off a salesman for pushing leftover stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting' moves R, the first of 'remnants', to the front of OVER, giving ROVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprove is to rebuke or scold, a synonym.

clue.text: Pan with grouse, feature of Sunday lunch?

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, to roast
to grouse is to complain, to beef

explanation.surface: A frying pan and a game bird for a Sunday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' and 'grouse' look like cookware and game; both are verbs for criticising and complaining.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British Sunday lunch is often centred on a roasted joint of meat.

clue.text: Dear Miss Piggy perhaps and Kermit finally up for a dance

indicators.note: up in a down answer means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: pet is a term of endearment, like dear
Miss Piggy is a pig, a female one being a sow

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of Kermit

explanation.surface: The Muppets Miss Piggy and Kermit get up to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses PET + SOW + T in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-step is a ballroom dance.

clue.text: Child of the '60s briefly joins in faction striking

indicators.note: joins in means goes inside the faction

parts.note: a wing is a faction of a party

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: a hippy is a member of the 1960s counterculture

explanation.surface: A 1960s flower child joins a faction on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' looks like taking industrial action; it means hitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Whipping is striking with a lash or cane, a synonym.

clue.text: Plant, one a pretentious sort brought from the east

indicators.note: in an across answer, from the east means read right to left

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a snob is a pretentious person

explanation.surface: A snob imports a plant from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought from the east' reverses I + A + SNOB.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a miniature tree grown in a pot, a type of plant.

clue.text: Small supermarket supplying some ice cream

parts.note: the Co-op is a British supermarket chain

explanation.surface: A little shop sells ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: The Co-op is a British cooperative supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion of ice cream served with a rounded spoon is a measure of some.

clue.text: Unruly lord of the Caribbean?

parts.note: WI is the West Indies, the Caribbean islands

explanation.surface: An undisciplined aristocrat in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Unruly and wild both mean uncontrolled, synonyms.

clue.text: Thick-skinned type sounding witty? Wrong

indicators.note: sounding means we want words that sound like these

parts.note: wry means drily witty, and 'no' answers the question by saying it is wrong

explanation.surface: Is a thick-skinned person witty? No.
explanation.walkthrough: WRY NO said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhinoceros has very tough hide, an animal example of thick skin.

clue.text: Drama in old hospital, nursing a broken joint

indicators.note: nursing means holding, so these go inside the hospital

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A medical drama set in an old hospital treating a broken joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the joint into INTJO, and 'nursing' puts A and that inside the sanatorium.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Joan is a play by George Bernard Shaw.

clue.text: Snacked regularly at bar, entertained by pop musicians

indicators.note: entertained by means held inside the father

parts.note: pop is an informal word for a father

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter

parts.note: to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: Musicians snacked at a bar while their father hosted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters, NCE. 'pop' looks like music; it is father.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance band is a group of musicians playing for dancing.

clue.text: Writer looks for an audience

indicators.note: for an audience means spoken aloud to listeners

parts.note: peeps are quick looks

explanation.surface: An author seeks readers.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Pepys was the 17th-century English diarist.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepys wrote the famous diary of Restoration London.
